```{r, include = FALSE}
# chunks run on the example file shipped with the package
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  eval = TRUE)
```

**pod5R** reads POD5 files produced by Oxford Nanopore sequencing devices, using the native POD5 C API. Read metadata, sequencing run information, and raw or calibrated signals are returned as ordinary R data frames, lists, and vectors. Python, reticulate, and the R Arrow package are not needed.

This vignette gives a short overview of the main functions. Signal extraction and plotting are covered in `vignette("signal_extraction")`, and plotting of many reads in `vignette("batch_plotting")`. Installation instructions can be found in the [README](https://github.com/LRB-IIMCB/pod5R#installation).

> **Note:** pod5R provides read-only access. It does not write POD5 files, segment the signal, or perform basecalling.

## Example data

All examples use a small toy direct RNA sequencing (DRS) file provided with the package. The same calls work for any POD5 file.

```{r example-file}
pod5_file <- system.file("extdata", "drs-filtered.pod5",
                         package = "pod5R", mustWork = TRUE)
```

## File information

`read_pod5_info()` returns file-level information: the file identifier, the format version, and the number of reads, batches, and runs.

```{r file-info}
pod5R::read_pod5_info(pod5_file)
```

## Read identifiers

`read_pod5_ids()` returns read identifiers (UUIDs) in file order. No signal data are decompressed at this step.

```{r read-ids}
read_ids <- pod5R::read_pod5_ids(pod5_file)

length(read_ids)
head(read_ids, 3)
```


## Read metadata

`read_pod5()` returns one row of metadata per read. Unless `signal = TRUE` is set, the signal data are not decompressed, so even large files are scanned quickly.

```{r read-metadata}
reads <- pod5R::read_pod5(pod5_file)

head(reads[, c("read_id", "num_samples", "sample_rate", "end_reason")], 3)
```


Run-level information, such as the flow cell, kit, and sample rate, are available through `read_pod5_runs()`:

```{r read-runs}
runs <- pod5R::read_pod5_runs(pod5_file)

names(runs)
```


## Signal

`extract_pod5_signal()` returns a list of signal vectors named by read UUID. Raw signals are integer ADC counts. With `calibrated = TRUE`, the signals are returned in picoamperes (pA) instead.

```{r signal}
signal_list <- pod5R::extract_pod5_signal(pod5_file,
                                          read_ids = read_ids[1],
                                          calibrated = TRUE)

str(signal_list)
```

## Reusing a reader

Every call with a file path opens and closes the file. Since opening visits every read batch, it is recommended to open a reader once with `open_pod5()` when several calls are made on the same file, reusing it, and closing it with `close_pod5()` at the end. Be aware that readers cannot be shared between parallel R workers, each worker should open its own reader.

```{r reader}
reader <- pod5R::open_pod5(pod5_file)

n_reads <- pod5R::read_pod5_info(reader)$num_reads
first_signal <- pod5R::extract_pod5_signal(reader, read_ids = read_ids[1])

pod5R::close_pod5(reader)

n_reads
length(first_signal[[1]])
```

| Topic | Vignette |
|---|---|
| Signal extraction, intervals, calibration, and plotting of single reads | `vignette("signal_extraction")` |
| Plotting many reads in one figure or one file per read | `vignette("batch_plotting")` |

| Function | Description |
|---|---|
| `read_pod5_info()` | File-level information |
| `read_pod5_ids()` | Read identifiers in file order |
| `read_pod5()` | Read metadata; signal with `signal = TRUE` |
| `read_pod5_runs()` | Sequencing run information |
| `extract_pod5_signal()` | Raw or calibrated signal vectors |
| `extract_pod5_signal_dorado()` | Signal intervals of Dorado split reads |
| `process_pod5()` | Processing of reads in groups |
| `open_pod5()` / `close_pod5()` | Opening and closing of a reusable reader |
